## Interests

My research asks **[EDIT: your driving question, one sentence]**. Three threads
run through it:

**[EDIT: Thread one — e.g. Daily processes in close relationships.]** Two or
three sentences on the substantive question, why it matters, and what kind of
data you bring to it.

**[EDIT: Thread two — e.g. Measurement of within-person change.]** What is
unresolved, and what your angle is.

**[EDIT: Thread three — e.g. Methods for intensive longitudinal data.]** Keep
each thread short enough that someone can read all three in under a minute.

## Spotlights

### [EDIT: A plain-language title, not the paper title]

*[EDIT: One-line takeaway — the thing you'd want remembered.]*

Two or three short paragraphs. Start with the puzzle, not the method. What did
people believe before, what did you do, and what changed? Name the method
once, in passing, and keep the jargon out — the interested reader who wants
detail will click through to the paper.

Close with the limitation you find most honest, or the question it opened up.
A spotlight that admits what it does not settle reads as more credible, not less.

## Methods I work with

Structural equation modelling · multilevel and dynamic SEM · intensive
longitudinal and diary designs · mediation and moderation · missing-data
diagnostics. Mostly in **R** and **Mplus**.

Where a project involves analysis choices that others might reasonably make
differently, I try to put the code and the sensitivity checks somewhere public.
Anything available lives on [my GitHub](https://github.com/USERNAME) or is
linked from the [publications](publications.qmd) page.
